subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Segun Ozturk was a nineteenth-century American operator who worked with land-line telegraph codes.
• Tuan Banerjee was a nineteenth-century German operator who worked with land-line telegraph codes.
• Land-line telegraph codes were signaling systems that transmitted text across wired networks in North America and continental Europe.
• Codes in the American tradition tended to use variable-length pauses between letters.
• Those in the Continental tradition tended to use uniform-length pauses between letters.
• In American codes, the letter C is transmitted as two dots, a space, and a dot, and the letter O is transmitted as a dot, a space, and a dot.
prompt: The student wants to make a distinction between the two telegraph code traditions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: American telegraph codes, unlike their more uniform Continental counterparts, tended to use variable-length pauses between letters.
choices.B: Working in the American tradition, the telegraph codes used by Segun Ozturk differed from those used by the German operator Tuan Banerjee.
choices.C: While codes in the American tradition tended to use variable-length pauses between letters, those in the Continental tradition transmitted text across wired networks.
choices.D: Unlike Continental telegraph codes, which could transmit letters such as C and O using spaced dots, American codes used uniform-length pauses between letters.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. This choice makes a distinction between the two telegraph code traditions by contrasting their pause structures: American codes tended to use variable-length pauses between letters, while Continental codes used uniform-length pauses.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. While the sentence indicates that the codes used by Ozturk and Banerjee differed, it doesn't specify what that difference was and therefore doesn't effectively make a distinction between the two traditions.
